item.title: Iran and US agree on 'guiding principles' in Geneva nuclear talks
item.description:
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held discussions with International Atomic Energy Agency Director General Rafael Grossi in Geneva on Monday, hours before resuming indirect nuclear negotiations with the United States. The meeting addressed technical nuclear issues as the UN watchdog continues pressing Tehran for clarity on its uranium stockpile and access to facilities damaged in US and Israeli strikes last year.

Grossi confirmed the session on social media platform X, writing that he had completed "in-depth technical discussions" with Araghchi "in preparation for important negotiations scheduled for tomorrow." The encounter took place at Araghchi's accommodation in Geneva, according to Iran's Foreign Ministry, which stated the two exchanged views on cooperation between Iran and the IAEA within the framework of safeguards obligations.

item.title: UK MPs to consider investigation into Andrew over Epstein leaks
item.description:
British Members of Parliament could launch an investigation into Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's decade-long tenure as a UK trade envoy as early as next week, after newly released documents from the U.S. Justice Department revealed he allegedly shared confidential government briefings with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Liam Byrne, chairman of the cross-party Business and Trade Committee, told reporters on Monday that "nothing is off the table" as lawmakers prepare to consider how to proceed when they meet next Tuesday. The development marks a major escalation in scrutiny of the former prince, who already faces a police assessment over potential misconduct in public office.

item.title: India confirms seizure of Iran-linked tankers, deploys 55 ships
item.description: India has seized three US-sanctioned oil tankers suspected of ties to Iran's shadow fleet, confirming the country's first major enforcement action against vessels evading international sanctions. The operation, which comes amid improving US-India relations following a bilateral trade deal, has prompted an expanded maritime surveillance effort by the Indian Coast Guard.

item.title: Ukraine hits Russian oil refinery as peace talks open in Geneva
item.description:
Ukrainian drones struck multiple regions across Russia overnight on February 17, targeting oil infrastructure and triggering airport closures in what Russian-installed authorities in Crimea described as one of the longest attacks in recent times. The wave of strikes came as Russian and Ukrainian delegations convened in Geneva for a new round of U.S.-brokered peace talks.

Russia's Defense Ministry reported that air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 151 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones overnight, with strikes reaching deep into Russian territory. The attacks targeted regions from Crimea in the south to Tatarstan in central Russia, approximately 1,300 kilometers from the front lines.

item.title: Trump says he's discussing Taiwan arms sales with Xi
item.description:
President Donald Trump acknowledged he has been in direct discussions with Chinese President Xi Jinping regarding US weapons sales to Taiwan, telling reporters aboard Air Force One on February 16 that he would reach a decision "pretty soon." The admission has drawn scrutiny from foreign policy observers, as it appears to contradict the Reagan-era Six Assurances, which commit Washington not to consult with Beijing on arms transfers to the self-governing island.

"I'm talking to him about it. We had a good conversation, and we'll make a determination pretty soon," Trump said, emphasizing his "good relationship" with Xi ahead of a planned April summit in Beijing.

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 4.6 with 1M token context window
item.description:
Anthropic unveiled Claude Sonnet 4.6 on Tuesday, bringing its most capable mid-tier AI model to users across all subscription levels, including free accounts. The release arrives just weeks after the company launched its flagship Opus 4.6 model in early February.

The updated Sonnet model delivers advances in coding, computer use, long-context reasoning, and agent planning. Most notably, it introduces a 1 million token context window in beta, allowing the model to process entire codebases, lengthy contracts, or dozens of research papers in a single request.

item.title: Emails reveal Epstein called himself 'Davos concierge' for elites
item.description:
Jeffrey Epstein leveraged the World Economic Forum's annual gathering in Switzerland to trade influence and arrange meetings between some of the world's most powerful figures, despite claiming to "hate" the forum, according to emails released by the U.S. Department of Justice and a trove of messages from Epstein's Yahoo account obtained by Bloomberg.

The disgraced financier, who died in 2019 while awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges, described himself as a "Davos concierge," offering to help contacts navigate the exclusive conference by securing accommodations in a venue where lodging is scarce and promising to arrange meetings with billionaires and government officials, Bloomberg reported Monday. It remains unclear how many times, if at all, Epstein actually attended the event — the World Economic Forum declined to comment on the matter.

item.title: Oil tanker breaks Cuba's five-week fuel drought amid US blockade
item.description:
The tanker Nicos I.V. entered Cuba's Matanzas Bay on February 16, becoming the first vessel to deliver fuel to the island in more than five weeks as the country struggles through its worst energy crisis since the collapse of the Soviet Union.

The 183-meter vessel, flying the flag of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, docked at Cuba's main energy logistics hub appearing partially loaded, according to maritime monitoring data and reports from El Independiente. While the ship has capacity for more than 300,000 barrels, neither the type nor volume of fuel it carried has been disclosed. If confirmed to have originated from a foreign port, it would be the first international delivery since the Ocean Mariner arrived from Mexico on January 9 with approximately 85,000 barrels, Bloomberg reported at the time.

item.title: Scientists trace Antarctica's 'gravity hole' to 70 million years of deep Earth shifts
item.description:
A pair of studies released this month is reshaping scientific understanding of Antarctica's past and future, linking slow-moving forces deep inside the planet to the fate of its massive ice sheets.

Researchers have traced the origins of the so-called Antarctic "gravity hole"—Earth's strongest gravitational anomaly—to rock movements occurring over tens of millions of years, while an international team has recovered a record-breaking sediment core from beneath the ice that spans 23 million years of climate history.

item.title: Russia, China, Iran deploy ships for joint drills in Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
Russia, China, and Iran have deployed naval vessels to the Strait of Hormuz for joint military exercises, according to an announcement Tuesday by Russian presidential aide Nikolai Patrushev.

In an interview with the Russian weekly Argumenty i Fakty, Patrushev said the "Maritime Security Belt 2026" exercises in the strategically vital waterway "proved to be relevant," describing the drills as part of Moscow's effort to build a "multipolar world order on the oceans" in response to what he characterized as Western hegemony. The exercises represent the eighth iteration of the Maritime Security Belt drills, which have been held since 2019 at the initiative of Iran's navy.

item.title: Peru's Congress ousts President Jeri over Chinese meeting scandal
item.description:
Peru's Congress on Tuesday voted to remove President Jose Jeri from office after just four months, continuing the Andean nation's revolving door of leaders amid a scandal over secret meetings with Chinese businessmen.

Lawmakers voted 75-24 to censure Jeri, stripping him of his title as president of Congress and effectively ending his brief presidency. The removal makes him Peru's eighth head of state in less than a decade, and the third consecutive president to be ousted from office.

item.title: US-mediated Ukraine-Russia talks end first day with no progress
item.description:
Negotiators from Ukraine and Russia completed a tense first day of US-mediated peace talks in Geneva on Tuesday, with neither side signaling progress on ending Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II. The discussions, scheduled to continue Wednesday, come just one week before the fourth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

"They were very tense. They lasted six hours. They have now concluded. It has been agreed to continue tomorrow," a source close to the Russian delegation told reporters. The negotiations unfolded in various bilateral and trilateral formats, according to Reuters.

item.title: Study finds climate change intensified Valencia's deadly 2024 floods
item.description:
A study published this week in Nature Communications has concluded that human-caused climate change substantially amplified the catastrophic flash floods that struck Valencia, Spain in October 2024, killing 230 people in one of the deadliest natural disasters in modern Spanish history.

The research, led by scientists from several Spanish research centers, found that present-day global warming conditions increased precipitation intensity by 21 percent over a six-hour period compared to what would have occurred in pre-industrial times. The study also determined that climate change expanded the area receiving more than 180 millimeters of rain by 55 percent and raised total rainfall volume in the Júcar River basin by 19 percent.

item.title: Ramadan begins in Gaza amid fragile ceasefire and muted spirit
item.description:
Palestinians in Gaza prepare to observe Ramadan beginning Wednesday under a tenuous ceasefire agreement, but the weight of war losses and grinding daily hardships have muted the spirit typically associated with the Muslim holy month.

"There is no joy. We lost family and loved ones," Fedaa Ayyad, a Gaza City resident, told the Associated Press. "Even if we attempt to adapt to the situation, we can't genuinely feel it in our hearts. I am one of those who cannot sense the spirit of Ramadan."

The holy month, normally a time for family gatherings, spiritual reflection, and acts of charity, arrives as Gaza endures its third consecutive Ramadan under the shadow of Israel's military campaign, which has killed more than 72,000 Palestinians—mostly women and children—and injured over 171,000 since October 2023.

item.title: US and Iran reach 'guiding principles' in Geneva nuclear talks
item.description:
U.S. stock markets closed with modest gains on Tuesday as investors balanced easing geopolitical tensions from progress in U.S.-Iran nuclear talks against persistent concerns about artificial intelligence disrupting traditional industries. Gold fell more than 2% as safe-haven demand weakened following signs of diplomatic progress in Geneva.

The S&P 500 rose 0.1% to 6,843.22 after swinging between a gain of 0.5% and a loss of nearly 1% during a volatile session, according to the Associated Press. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and Nasdaq Composite also each gained 0.1%, with trading volumes reduced following Monday's Presidents' Day holiday.

item.title: Japan's parliament set to reappoint Takaichi as prime minister
item.description:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is set to be reappointed on Wednesday following her landslide election victory on February 8, which gave her Liberal Democratic Party a historic two-thirds supermajority in the lower house of parliament. Though the reappointment is largely ceremonial, Takaichi intends to leverage the day's symbolism to advance her conservative agenda on defense, immigration, and social policy.

The LDP won 316 of the 465 seats in the powerful lower house—its biggest electoral triumph in the party's seven-decade history, according to public broadcaster NHK. Together with its coalition partner, the Japan Innovation Party, the ruling bloc commands 352 seats. This supermajority gives Takaichi the ability to override opposition vetoes in the upper house, where the coalition lacks a majority.

item.title: Cambodia says Thai forces occupy its territory despite ceasefire
item.description:
Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet said Tuesday that Thai military forces are occupying portions of Cambodian land following armed clashes last year, despite a peace agreement signed in late December, urging Thailand to permit a joint boundary commission to begin demarcation work along the disputed 817-kilometer border.

Speaking to Reuters during his visit to Washington ahead of Trump's Board of Peace inaugural meeting on February 19, Hun Manet described the border situation as "fragile" even after a ceasefire was declared on December 27, bringing an end to the most severe fighting between the two nations in over a decade.

item.title: Rolls-Royce hybrid aircraft engine to be tested in France this summer
item.description:
Rolls-Royce and Norwegian research organization SINTEF are developing a hybrid aircraft engine that could reduce aviation CO₂ emissions by up to 30 percent, with a demonstration engine set to be tested in France this summer and commercial deployment targeted for 2035.

The engine, being developed as part of the EU-funded He-Art project, combines an electric motor with a traditional combustion engine to power a propeller, applying technology similar to that used in hybrid automobiles to the aviation sector.

"The principle that causes emissions to decrease is the same as for hybrid cars—that is, a combination of both fuel and electricity," said SINTEF researcher Torstein Grav Aakre.

item.title: Greenland dog sled champion sees first snowless January in memory
item.description:
In the Arctic town of Ilulissat, 186 miles north of the Arctic Circle, five-time Greenlandic dog sled champion Jørgen Kristensen is witnessing something he has never seen before: a January without snow or ice in the bay.

Instead of gliding across frozen terrain, Kristensen's sled now bounces over exposed earth and rock. Temperatures that were once reliably frigid now climb above freezing, sometimes reaching 10 degrees Celsius (50 Fahrenheit)—conditions that make traditional dog sledding increasingly impossible. For more than a thousand years, sled dogs have been integral to Inuit hunters and fishermen traversing the Arctic. That way of life is now under threat.

"If we lose the dog sledding, we have large parts of our culture that we're losing. That scares me," Kristensen told the Associated Press, becoming visibly emotional.

item.title: Climate change adds 47 extra harmful heat days to coffee regions
item.description: Two new analyses released this week warn that rising temperatures and extreme weather driven by climate change are increasingly endangering coffee and wheat production worldwide, with implications for both farmers and consumers.
